messages:
alex.p: Heads up — customer AcmeHealth escalated: intermittent 3–8s latencies on generate endpoints. Traced to downstream KMS Decrypt calls that sometimes return AccessDenied then succeed on retry. Proxy CPU spikes at same times. Also noticed some Decrypt CloudTrail events are missing for the same time windows. Sharing logs below.

kim: Can you paste the request IDs + sample logs? Also which proxy version is in front of KMS for AcmeHealth?

nate.s: snippet from app logs (filtered):
```
2026-03-10T18:12:02Z request_id=01F7XQ Decrypt start encctx_present=false
2026-03-10T18:12:02Z request_id=01F7XQ KMS_RESP AccessDenied
2026-03-10T18:12:03Z request_id=01F7XQ retry=1 -> KMS_RESP Success key_id=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123:key/abcd
2026-03-10T18:12:02Z request_id=01F7Y Decrypt start encctx_present=true
2026-03-10T18:12:02Z request_id=01F7Y KMS_RESP Success
```
```
proxy metrics around 18:12:02: cpu 89%, epoll queue growing, http2 stream resets + some headers dropped
```

support-ops: Customer also flagged a billing spike (extra decrypts due to retries). They want ETA on resolution and whether we can refund the extra usage while investigating.

security-oncall-bot: @oncall assigned -> alex.p (primary), kim (backup). Incident ticket INC-2026-321 created: https://redwood/ops/incidents/INC-2026-321

hsm-proxy: quick note — proxy v2.4.1 has a known regression with gRPC/HTTP2 header fragmentation: under high concurrency the proxy may not reassemble custom headers > 256 bytes reliably, causing some x-kms-encctx headers to be seen as missing. That matches encctx_present=false above. Workarounds: (1) enable header-preservation flag in proxy config or (2) roll back to 2.3.x. We have a 2.4.2 patch that fixes the frame handling; ETA to cut CI + canary is ~2 hours.

kim: good find. Does the customer use our JS SDK with auto-metadata (we inject encctx header) or do they set encryptionContext manually?

alex.p: they use our hosted SDK which injects encctx as a custom header (x-kms-encctx) via the edge. So it traverses the proxy.

nate.s: repro steps I used locally (quick):
```
# simulate missing encctx
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "x-kms-encctx: {\"owner\":\"acme\"}" \
  --http2 https://edge.redwood.ai/v1/decrypt
# then hit a loop of high concurrency using hey or wrk to reproduce header drop
```
Result: when proxy drops header, KMS returns AccessDenied because our key policy has Condition StringEquals on encryption context owner.

support-ops: Proposed mitigations for customer impact:
- short-term: scale proxy pool for AcmeHealth to reduce frame fragmentation risk (horizontal pods + lower concurrency per pod)
- immediate: enable header-preservation flag on their proxy config (non-disruptive)
- mid-term: push 2.4.2 patch to canary and then rollout
- billing: recommend refund for duplicate decrypt unit usage during window; ops to approve

kim: technical checklist to gather before patch:
1) collect proxy logs + tcpdump for a small window (I can provide tcpdump command)
2) collect CloudTrail lookup for Decrypt events (note: CloudTrail sampling/aggregation could make some events appear delayed)
3) capture KMS request ids (x-amz-request-id) from app logs and proxy logs
4) verify key policy condition that requires specific encryption context keys (owner, env)

alex.p: tcpdump command I used:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/kms-proxy.pcap host kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com and port 443
# then extract TLS record side for a short window with tshark to see headers on our side
```
I'll collect 2 minutes around next spike and attach to INC-2026-321.

hsm-proxy: patch plan: we will cut a 2.4.2 release containing the frame reassembly fix and a defensive check that logs when expected custom headers are truncated. CI + canary in our staging cluster within ~2 hours, full rollout after 3 successful canaries. I'll post the commit and canary link here when ready.

nate.s: additional thought — if key policy is strict (Condition on encryption context) we should consider a temporary soft-fail path in edge that returns a 5xx upstream-consent error (and not retry) to avoid double-decrypt billing while we fix the header. That would surface an app error rather than trigger KMS retries. Thoughts?

kim: I like that. Implement short-lived change: edge will detect missing encctx and return 400 with clear message instead of letting client retry automatically. We'll need to coordinate with SDK teams so they don't auto-retry blindly.

support-ops: I'll draft customer comms: acknowledging root cause hypothesis (proxy header drop), mitigation plan (enable header-preservation, patch rollout), ETA, and billing remediation. Will ask for formal refund approval from finance.

alex.p: assigning owners:
- collect pcap + request ids -> alex.p (me)
- enable header-preservation flag -> support-ops / infra config (kim to coordinate)
- cut + canary 2.4.2 -> hsm-proxy
- edge short-lived missing-encctx 400 behavior -> kim / eng-runtime
- customer comms + billing -> support-ops

Please update INC-2026-321 with progress.

security-oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-321 status updated: triage -> investigating. Incident doc: https://redwood/ops/incidents/INC-2026-321/doc

hsm-proxy: patch uploaded: commit bc3a9f, canary URL: https://ci.redwood/canaries/hsm-proxy/2.4.2/1. Starting canary in 10m.

alex.p: thanks everyone. I'll attach pcap and app logs as soon as I have them. If we see another spike in the meantime, please react here and @alex.p. :thumbsup:
